text:
UMaine Extension to host urban soil safety workshop in Brewer on August 6
The University of Maine Cooperative Extension announced on July 14 that it will host a workshop focused on best practices for growing food safely in urban soils. The event is scheduled for Thursday, August 6, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at 20 Ivers Street in Brewer and is co-hosted with Food and Medicine, Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Organization, American Farmland Trust, and Weezy’s Farm and Flowers.
Urban farmers and gardeners attending the workshop will participate in activities and discussions about potential contaminants found in urban soils. Sessions are designed to help growers interpret risk, amend their soils, build raised beds, and understand the history of lead contamination. Partner organizations will provide information tables covering topics such as sustainable urban growing practices, soil testing resources, and upcoming community events.
Refreshments will be available at the free event. Registration is requested through the Grow Food Safely in Urban Soils event page. For further information or reasonable accommodation requests, attendees can contact Carrick Gambell by email or phone.
The University of Maine Cooperative Extension supports community engagement through volunteer programs and educational events that connect people with shared interests; it also runs the Diagnostic and Research Laboratory—including veterinary, pest management, and aquatic health units—and produces a weekly podcast called The Maine Farmcast featuring expert discussions for farmers. These efforts extend throughout Maine as part of its mission to deliver research-backed solutions for individuals, businesses, and communities addressing local issues or opportunities, according to the official website.
Extension has operated as a resource supporting UMaine’s land- and sea-grant public education role for over a century by conducting community-driven programs across all counties in Maine.
